attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this assessment in his own words.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves his retrospective assessment, with the 26-month period retained as a qualifier.

contract.note: Reading unresolved problems as persistent hallucinations and unreliability is ordinary and grounded in the surrounding text. The contract appropriately excludes the separate assertion about alignment progress.

evidence.note: OpenAI's contemporaneous company disclosure acknowledges factual hallucinations and reasoning errors in GPT-4 during the target period.
Google acknowledges inaccurate AI Overviews immediately before the post. This supports persistent reliability problems, while its qualifications limit conclusions about their prevalence.
The independent May 2024 evaluation finds substantial residual hallucinations in commercial legal AI tools. Its domain-specific rates should not be generalized to all uses.
OpenAI reports improved factuality on an internal benchmark. Improvement does not establish resolution, and the passage explicitly acknowledges remaining hallucinations.

reviews.rationale: Company disclosures and independent testing show that hallucinations and unreliability persisted through May 2024. Reported improvements do not contradict the narrower claim that these problems remained unresolved. This finding does not establish an absence of progress or adjudicate the separate alignment assertion.
